meta.title: The People v. Ansel Roarke
meta.tone: Airless, procedural, and running out of time.
content_rules: No scene ever leaves the courtroom. Recesses happen off the page.

style: Every scene is testimony, objection, or the silence between them.
The room never changes, so specificity comes from people - a witness's hands, a juror's attention wandering.
Never narrate what happens outside this room. If it matters, someone says it under oath.

world.setting_summary: Courtroom 4B, day six of eight. The prosecution has rested. You have not.
rules: The story never leaves the courtroom. No flashback, no corridor, no chambers.
The judge's patience is finite and visibly spending itself.
A witness who has already testified cannot be recalled.

Judge Imelda Sarris.name: Judge Imelda Sarris
Judge Imelda Sarris.description: Thirty years on the bench and a settled contempt for theatre that does not extend to being bored.
Judge Imelda Sarris.relationship_to_player: neutral, and audibly less so each time you push
Judge Imelda Sarris.hook: Asking, without raising her voice, where exactly this is going

revelations.trigger: A witness contradicts a detail of their own earlier statement, on the record.
revelations.content: It is small, and it is fatal, and you are the only person in the room who has both versions in front of them.

revelations.trigger: The protagonist enters a physical exhibit into evidence.
revelations.content: The moment it is in your hand you understand why the prosecution never entered it themselves.

failure_conditions.trigger: The protagonist defies a direct ruling from the bench for the third time.
failure_conditions.title: Removed From the Record
failure_conditions.ending_prompt: Close in the corridor, disbarred from this room at least, with the trial continuing audibly without you.

failure_conditions.trigger: The protagonist rests the defence without ever impeaching a prosecution witness.
failure_conditions.title: Nothing Further
failure_conditions.ending_prompt: Close on the verdict, read into a room that has already stopped listening.

main_thread.title: Reasonable Doubt
main_thread.description: Raise it, in this room, before the bench runs out of patience.

acts.title: The Defence Opens
acts.description: Your first witness. Everything the jury believes for the rest of the trial is decided in the next hour.
completion_signals: A prosecution account has been impeached on the record

initial_scene.summary: The prosecution has rested. The judge is waiting for the protagonist to stand.

opening_scene.narration_before_name: The clerk needs the name for the record, and asks twice, because the first time you did not answer.
opening_scene.narration_after_name:
"{player_name}. For the defence." The clerk writes it down. Judge Sarris looks at the clock, then at you.

OPTIONS:
1. Calls the first defence witness || I stand and call the witness I have been saving, and hope she is still willing.
2. Moves for dismissal before calling anyone || I move to dismiss, knowing it fails, because I want to hear how she says no.
3. Asks the bench for a short recess || I ask for ten minutes, and let the room see me ask.
